anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: MNE-BIDS is a software tool for organizing electrophysiological data into BIDS, used to format this dataset; it does not describe the Gloups MEG data.

anchors.paper_title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
anchors.reason: MEG-BIDS is a data-organization standard specification used to format this MEG dataset, not a paper describing the Gloups_MEG learning-task data.

metadata.methods_description: MEG data were acquired using a 4D NeuroImaging system with 248 magnetometer channels. Participants completed a learning task and a resting-state condition during recording. Data acquisition was performed at the MEG Centre, Timone Hospital, Marseille, France.

citation_details.title: Dataset for Evaluating the Production of Phonotactically Legal and Illegal Pseudowords
citation_details.author: Valérie Chanoine, Snežana Todorović, Bruno Nazarian, Jean‐Michel Badier, Khoubeib Kanzari, Andrea Brovelli, Sonja A. Kotz, Elin Runnqvist
citation_details.abstract: The "MEG-GLOUPS" dataset offers a curated collection of raw magnetoencephalography recordings from seventeen French participants engaged in a pseudoword learning task as well as resting-state activity before and after the task. A dataset called Gloups with the same participants and a similar learning task adapted to functional magnetic resonance imaging is already available. In the learning task, participants were instructed to pronounce monosyllabic pseudowords, which were presented both visually and auditorily. These pseudowords were either phonotactically legal or illegal in the participants' native language, French. We organized the dataset according to the Brain Imaging Data Structure (BIDS), pre-processed the data and performed a minimal analysis of Event-Related Fields (ERFs), to ensure data quality and integrity of the dataset. This data collection includes comprehensive descriptions of the theoretical background, methods, data recordings, and technical validation.

citation_details.title: Gloups_MEG
citation_details.author: Snežana Todorović, Elin Runnqvist, Valerie Chanoine, Jean‐Michel Badier
citation_details.abstract: This magnetoencephalography (MEG) dataset comprises recordings from 17 adult participants performing a learning task and resting-state condition using a 4D NeuroImaging system with 248 magnetometer channels. This is a NEMAR-hosted version of OpenNeuro dataset ds005261 (v2.0.0), part of a multimodal neuroimaging study investigating speech sequence production and phonotactic constraints. The MEG recordings provide complementary temporal resolution for understanding cortico-cerebellar mechanisms underlying speech production. Related fMRI data from the same participants are available in OpenNeuro dataset ds004597.
